target_customer: Patients with chronic or rare conditions, and pharma sponsors and research organizations paying for real-world data and trial support
problem: Patients' medical records are scattered across providers, making care coordination and research hard.
business_model: Started as a consumer records service; now B2B real-world data and clinical research services for pharma
product_category: Health records and AI-enabled clinical research data

founders.name: Noga Leviner
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CEO. A secondary report says Luna Federici later became CEO and Leviner moved to the board; date not read.

founders.name: Troy Astorino
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CTO; still listed as co-founder and CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieving, digitizing and structuring records from many providers with HIPAA compliance, later with machine learning, was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Patient consented record datasets and provider retrieval operations compound over time, but it took years to build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired it; PicnicHealth itself bought rare disease platform AllStripes in October 2023.

market_need_then: Patients' records were fragmented across providers, with the 2015 TechCrunch seed coverage describing a virtual records platform.

identity.logo: A P symbol with a cross representing medicine, per a third-party design critique

branding.brand_signature: A warm, patient-friendly name in a clinical field

rebrands.why: Parent company renamed to reflect AI focus, per a rebrand release; PicnicHealth kept as patient brand and PicnicResearch added for pharma

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive, friendly name that stands out in healthcare, with press for funding rounds and a deliberate multi-brand rebrand, but no evidence of community pull.

pivots.from: Consumer service collecting and organizing patients' records
pivots.to: Real-world data and clinical research provider for pharma sponsors
pivots.why: Series funding announcements describe building datasets for medical research; exact date not stated

outcome_analysis: PicnicHealth moved from a 2015 seed for a records service to a research data business, raising roughly 100 million dollars through a 2022 Series C led by B Capital, buying AllStripes in 2023 and renaming the parent PicnicAI in 2026. It remains independent, with CEO succession from co-founder Noga Leviner reported secondhand.
notes: Series A of 10M in 2018 and Series B amount of 25M come from search result summaries of press coverage; the Series B press release states a total above 35M. CB Insights lists 97.02M total over 9 rounds, which does not reconcile with rounds recorded; AllStripes seeds are separate. No dated 2014 competitor source was found, so the list is empty. The company site gave no founder or history detail.
